subject: Follow-up: DPA & SCC options + controller/processor alignment — AcuityPay
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@acuitypay.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Follow-up: DPA & SCC options + controller/processor alignment — AcuityPay

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — great conversation and very helpful context on AcuityPay's regulatory posture. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Compliance snapshot you shared: SOC 2 Type II in progress (expected report Q1 2027); HIPAA not in scope for AcuityPay's current product lines; GDPR applies for EU cardholders.
- AcuityPay ask: formal DPA + clarity on which SCC module we'll reference (processor-to-processor vs controller-to-processor mapping) and whether AcuityPay will need a controller-side addendum.
- Redwood posture: Hosted API with optional VPC Private deployment. We can be processor under a standard DPA; we offer SCC Module 2 (Processor) or Module 3 (Controller/Processor hybrid) depending on the role mapping.

Attachments I can share now: a short SOC 2 evidence summary (internal), and a draft DPA with two SCC module options flagged. I've attached a draft DPA and the SOC 2 summary for your legal/security team to review.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Please send the completed Vendor Security Questionnaire when convenient (we'll use it to map evidence gaps).
2) Legal/timebox: Can your team review our DPA draft and indicate preference for SCC module or suggest edits by Tue 24 Nov?
3) We'll run internal legal + infra to confirm any PKI/KMS requirements for the Private deployment if you choose that path (we can give a short checklist).

If useful, Jordan can join the next call to walk the SCC options and timeline.

Thanks — I left the attachments referenced below.

Best,
Monica
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0137

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Draft_AcuityPay_20261119.docx (draft), security-evidence-soc2-summary-2026-10.pdf
From: Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@acuitypay.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acuitypay.com>, security@acuitypay.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA & SCC options + controller/processor alignment — AcuityPay

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the clear recap. Attaching the Vendor Security Questionnaire you requested (filled). A few quick clarifications from our end:

- SOC 2: we're currently in an interim engagement and expect to have the Type II report available early Q1. For now our security team prefers evidence (policies + recent pen test) in lieu of the final report.
- Role mapping: AcuityPay will be controller for cardholder PII and a processor for aggregated tokenized telemetry we receive from partners. There may be a hybrid mapping depending on the dataset — we'd like Redwood to indicate which SCC module you recommend for each dataflow.
- HIPAA: not applicable today.

Can Jordan or Karthik coordinate with our security team on the questionnaire edge items (encryption-at-rest key ownership, KV cache persistence, and audit log retention)? Our security team included a few items as comments in the PDF.

Best,
Sara
Senior Legal Operations Manager | AcuityPay
sara.hughes@acuitypay.com

Attachment: AcuityPay_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_20261118.pdf
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@acuitypay.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 12:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA & SCC options + controller/processor alignment — AcuityPay

Sara — received, thanks for the questionnaire and the inline comments. Quick responses to your highlighted items (summary):

- Encryption/KMS: Redwood supports two options: customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) in Private deployments, or Redwood-managed KMS for Hosted. We'll flag the DPA draft with both options and note any changes to SLA for key-ownership scenarios.
- KV cache / token persistence: default runtime behavior retains ephemeral KV cache per session (not persisted to long-term storage). If you require longer retention for caching, we'd need to treat that dataflow as processor-storage and document it in the DPA/SCC mapping.
- Audit logs: 90 days retention on hosted by default; extended retention is available as an add-on and can be configured for Dedicated/Private.

Jordan and Karthik — can you take the security questionnaire comments and add a short section (2-3 bullets) for AcuityPay: recommended SCC module per dataflow and recommended KMS approach? If possible, we'll aim to return a redline of the DPA with those suggestions today so AcuityPay legal has something concrete.

I'll also schedule a 30-min follow-up for Fri 20 Nov to review — invite to follow.

Thanks,
Monica
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@acuitypay.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:31:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA & SCC options + controller/processor alignment — AcuityPay

Sara / Monica — looping in a short recommendation based on the questionnaire and today's notes:

- Dataflow A (cardholder PII from EU): AcuityPay = Controller, Redwood = Processor. Recommend SCC Module 2 (Processor) for that flow with explicit DPA Art. 28 mapping.
- Dataflow B (tokenized telemetry / aggregated signals): hybrid — both parties act as processors for partner-sourced telemetry, but AcuityPay may take controller responsibilities for derived identifiers. Recommend Module 3 (Controller/Processor hybrid) for the DPA appendix that covers analytics outputs.
- KMS recommendation: if you expect to retain tokenization keys under your control for compliance, request Private deployment with customer-managed KMS. Otherwise, Redwood-managed KMS is acceptable with SOC 2 evidence.

I've attached a marked-up DPA draft with comments on the SCC module choices and suggested language for audit log retention and KMS options. Monica — I added a 1-paragraph fallback we can use in case SOC 2 Type II isn't available at signing (conditional evidence acceptance).

Jordan
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

Jordan / Monica — thank you, this is very helpful and exactly the level of detail our legal/security teams need. Next actions from our side: 

1) We'll review the redline and confirm Module selections for both flows by Mon 23 Nov.
2) Security will validate the KMS approach; if we need customer-managed keys, we'll flag it in the redline.
3) We'll return any final edits to the DPA and sign-off plan; if SOC 2 report isn't available, AcuityPay legal is okay with the conditional evidence fallback Jordan proposed but will want a clear timeline in the DPA (target: provide Type II by 2027-03-31).

Can Monica send a calendar invite for a 30-min sync early next week to confirm sign-off owners and timeline? We'll aim to have Liam (Head of Payments) and one security SME join.

Thanks again — attaching a tiny screenshot reference (not required) of the question we annotated in the PDF.

Best,
Sara
